answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 222 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The inlet graph is validated at intake and the tide frontier is published, so that the ancestry of every answer is public, and terrace anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Honest users pay that once, farms 11 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
